records.text: Diligent Denison claimed that Mark Amodei was absent from the first two September 9 committee roll calls and first appeared on the third.

appearances.snippet: Diligent Denison on X Road exposed rep Mark Amodei tries and fails to give a solid alibi for the alleged September 9th meeting with Charlie Kirk's security Brian Harpole. ... However, he was not present for roll call until the third meeting in mid afternoon on the 9th in DC.

verification.notes: Official committee records substantiate that Amodei first appears on roll call 3. They do not establish that roll call 3 occurred in mid-afternoon, so that unsupported timing qualifier was removed from the migrated proposition.

records.text: The account This Is the Zero Hour accused Owens of tampering with evidence and claimed the person shown on the left was Diligent Denizen rather than Robinson.

appearances.snippet: This is the zero hour is what he goes by. He wrote, Candace Owens tampering with evidence. The man on the right is Tyler Robinson. ... The man on the left is diligent denizen. I will explain it all soon. Please do. Please do explain it all soon.

verification.notes: Search did not recover the original Zero Hour post or its promised explanation. The episode records the accusation, not proof of tampering or substitution. Owens's sarcastic reenactment wording is not an admission.

records.text: According to an Alaska Dog Lady comment read by Owens, Diligent Denizen jokingly said in an X Space that the figure resembled him more than Robinson, except for the skinny legs.
records.speaker: Diligent Denizen (online-investigator handle; identity unverified)

appearances.snippet: Trust him, bro. Just trust him, bro, or whatever. Yeah. Alaska dog lady writes. Bro, ironically, I was in diligent den space last night. He said jokingly, quote, this guy looks more like me than Tyler Robinson, except I don't have skinny legs.

verification.notes: This is a nested account through Alaska Dog Lady. Searches did not recover the original X Space recording or timestamp. The alleged joke is not an admission of substitution; neither the joke's original context nor the tampering accusation is independently established.
